title: Guess Who’s the Top Country Songwriter of All Time? It’s Not Who You Think!
summary: If I asked you to name the greatest country songwriter of all time, you might say Willie Nelson or Dolly Parton. But a brand-new study says the top spot actually belongs to someone you might not know: Ashley Gorley. He’s written huge hits like “I Had Some Help” and “I Am Not Okay.” Right behind him is Shane McAnally, who wrote “Body Like a Back Road” and “Mama’s Broken Heart.” The list was put together by a company called Record Research. They looked at every song that made the Billboard country charts from 1944 to 2025 and gave points based on how high and how long each song stayed on the chart. Because streaming lets songs pop up quickly now, modern writers like Gorley and McAnally have an advantage — they can rack up lots of hits in a short time. But don’t worry, some classic names are still in the top 10: Merle Haggard is No. 10, and Bill Anderson is No. 4. Most of the top writers aren’t famous singers themselves. They’re the behind-the-scenes heroes who craft the words and melodies that stars perform. The full top 40 list is in a new book called Top Country Singles 1944-2025, which comes out June 4 — just in time for CMA Fest in Nashville. The book’s publisher, Vinnie Freda, says charts aren’t about picking the “best” song, but about memories. A song that stays on the chart for weeks becomes part of our shared story. So next time you hear a country song you love, check who wrote it — you might be surprised!
why_it_matters: Next time you hear a catchy country song, you might think about the person who wrote the words — just like a book has an author, every song has a creator who might not be on stage.

background_read: Country music is known for its storytelling, and songwriters are the ones who weave those tales. Stars like Dolly Parton write their own songs, but many hits are created by professional behind-the-scenes writers like Ashley Gorley, who has written over 60 No. 1 singles. The Billboard charts have tracked the most popular country songs since 1944, and this new book uses that data to honor the writers who made songs stay in people’s memories.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ashley Gorley (top songwriter), Shane McAnally, and other writers, plus classic names like Merle Haggard.
WHAT: A ranking of the greatest country songwriters based on how high and how long their songs stayed on the Billboard country charts.
WHERE: The findings are published in a new book connected to Nashville’s CMA Fest.
WHY: To celebrate the unseen writers behind the hits and show that a song’s lasting chart life creates a shared story for everyone.
